DEFINITION · qeva:1:derivability@1

Derivability

The existence of a finite proof of a statement from declared assumptions under declared inference rules.

editoriallogic · proof · foundations
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Writing Gamma |- P means that P can be reached by a finite sequence of allowed proof steps from the declared axioms and premises.

EXACT

The compact statement

Gamma |-_{S} P means that there exists a finite S-valid derivation whose undischarged premises are permitted by Gamma and whose final formula is P.

Example

Whether a statement is derivable can change when axioms or inference rules change.

Boundary / caveat

Derivability is not identical to semantic truth. Soundness/completeness results relate the two only under stated hypotheses.

Assumptions

  • A formal system S and a set Gamma of admitted premises are fixed. · Formal system @1
